_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 3.7. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: Which are the three ways of committing fraud under the Fraud Act 2006?
options: False representation, failing to disclose information, abuse of position
Obtaining property, services and pecuniary advantage

questions.scenario: What is the maximum penalty for fraud (s. 1)?
D sends 1,000 phishing emails pretending to be a bank. Nobody responds. Which is correct?
options: Fraud by false representation is complete – no one needs to be deceived and no gain need be made

questions.scenario: When is a representation 'false' under s. 2?
options: If it is untrue or misleading and the maker knows it is, or might be, untrue or misleading

questions.scenario: D uses a stolen credit card to pay in a shop without saying anything. Is there a representation?
options: Yes – an implied representation that he has authority to use the card
Only if the card is declined

questions.scenario: D enters stolen card details on a website and an automated system accepts them. Can this be fraud by false representation?
options: Yes – a representation can be made to any system or device (s. 2(5))
No – a machine can't be deceived
Only if a human checks it

questions.scenario: A representation can be about…
options: Fact or law, including the state of mind of the person making it or any other person

questions.scenario: D orders a meal intending not to pay. Which fraud?
options: False representation – implied representation that he intends to pay
explanations: Correct (making off may also apply later).

questions.scenario: Under s. 5, 'gain' and 'loss' extend only to…
options: Money or other property, whether temporary or permanent
Anything of value, including sexual favours

questions.scenario: Does 'gain' include keeping what one already has?
A carer with access to an elderly man's bank account transfers money to herself. Which form of fraud fits best?
Can abuse of position (s. 4) be committed by omission?
Fraud by failing to disclose information (s. 3) requires…
options: A legal duty to disclose the information

questions.scenario: Following Ivey v Genting and R v Barton and Booth, the test for dishonesty is…
options: (1) D's actual state of knowledge or belief; (2) whether, given that, his conduct was dishonest by the standards of ordinary decent people
Only whether D thought he was honest
Whether D realised ordinary people would see it as dishonest
explanations: Old Ghosh second limb – no longer applies.

questions.scenario: Must D's belief about the facts be reasonable under the Ivey test?
options: No – but reasonableness is relevant to whether it was genuinely held

questions.scenario: D has a list of stolen card numbers on his laptop at home, intending to sell them for use in frauds. Which offence?
options: Possession of articles for use in frauds (s. 6) – and data counts as an article (s. 8)
explanations: s. 6 has no 'away from abode' limit.
Correct (s. 7 offering to supply may also apply).

questions.scenario: What is the maximum penalty for s. 6 (possession of articles)?
D designs and sells 'phishing kits' online. Which offence?
options: s. 7 – making, adapting, supplying or offering to supply articles for use in frauds

questions.scenario: D climbs over a fence into a football stadium to watch a match without paying. Which offence?
Which is required for s. 11 but NOT for s. 2?
options: That the services are actually obtained

questions.scenario: Can s. 11 be committed by omission?
options: No – it requires a dishonest act

questions.scenario: D lies on a job application about his qualifications to get a well-paid job. Which is correct?
options: Fraud by false representation – intending gain (salary) by a false representation
No gain – he must work for the salary

questions.scenario: D tells a buyer a used car has 'one careful owner' knowing it has had five. The buyer never relies on it. Is it fraud?
options: Only if the price was inflated
Yes – the false representation, with intent to gain, completes the offence

questions.scenario: A man uses a fake account to persuade a woman to sleep with him. Is this fraud?
options: No – gain/loss must relate to money or property
